title: Investigation snapshot playbook for output regressions & dashboard scripts
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for capturing a compact, reproducible investigation snapshot when an LLM output quality regression (or perceived latency/throughput regression tied to output) is reported. The aim is to get an operator or oncall from 0 -> 1: reproduce, collect the right telemetry (metrics + traces + artifacts), and spin up a narrow ad-hoc dashboard that answers the core hypotheses within 30–90 minutes.

When to use this doc:
- User or internal evaluation reports output drift (e.g., hallucinations, formatting regressions, tokenization artifacts)
- Sudden spike in downstream errors correlated with model rollouts
- Intermittent tenant reports of 'slower responses with same prompt' after a config change

High-level flow (compact):
1) Reproduce: get exact prompt + model version + routing path + headers
   - Ticket template first two fields: prompt text, seed/temperature/stop tokens, model-id, model-variant-tag, routing-policy-id, timestamp (iso).
   - If impossible to reproduce exactly, capture a small representative corpus (5–20 examples) and note divergence.
2) Snapshot traces and spans for the timeframe (±2 minutes):
   - Capture trace IDs for 3 symptomatic requests and 3 healthy baseline requests.
   - Export spans with full annotations: node_id, serving_pool, GPU_type, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, sequence_length, compile_kernel_version, quantization_profile.
3) Capture core metrics (30–90s window + aggregates):
   - token_latencies.p50/p90/p99 (by route, model, tenant)
   - request_errors.count and request_errors.type (parse: decode_error, model_oom, timeouts, bad_response)
   - kv_cache.hits / kv_cache.misses (per-tenant rolling window)
   - generation.quality.score (if we have eval heuristics; see below)
   - prompt_size.tokens and response_size.tokens distributions
   - routing.fallback.count and routing.model_switches (useful for graceful degradation)
4) Ad-hoc dashboard (30 min): minimal widgets to triage hypotheses
   - Widget A: Token latency quantiles (p50/p90/p99) over last 15m with tenant overlay
   - Widget B: Trace-sampled waterfall for 3 failing vs 3 healthy traces (side-by-side)
   - Widget C: KV cache warmth heatmap (last access per model shard)
   - Widget D: Model variant rollout timeline + % traffic and errors by variant
   - Widget E: Generation-quality quick sampling: 5 example prompts and outputs inline

Naming and metric contracts (short definitions to standardize captures):
- token_latencies.seconds: histogram of per-token generation latencies. Tags: model_id, model_variant, tenant_id, route, gpu_type, compile_kernel
- request_end_to_end.seconds: full request duration from API frontdoor to last token emitted. Tags: same as above + batch_id
- kv_cache_hitrate.rate: ratio of kv cache hits over requests touching KV. Tags: model_shard, tenant_id
- generation_quality.score: synthetic metric used in prod eval harness (0–1). Tags: eval_set, model_id
- trace_span.name: use canonical names: api.frontdoor -> router.route_decision -> serving.pool_queue -> serving.exec -> kvcache.lookup -> model.compile -> model.decode -> postprocess.filter

Trace tagging checklist (must be present on exported spans):
- trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id
- tenant_id, request_id, batch_id
- model_id, model_variant, kernel_signature, quant_profile
- kv_cache_hit (boolean), kv_cache_key_hint
- prompt_token_count, response_token_count, max_seq_len
- gpu_free_memory_mebibytes at span start (helpful for OOM patterns)

Investigation hypotheses & quick probes: (ordered by cost/impact)
H1: Model variant or rollout induced quality regression
  - Probe: compare generation_quality.score distribution across variants; sample outputs from each variant for same prompts.
H2: KV cache regression (evictions or namespace collision) causing slower generation
  - Probe: inspect kv_cache_hitrate.rate per tenant + last-touch heatmap; run warm-start synthetic probe for the model/tenant.
H3: Kernel or compiler change led to sticky slow paths
  - Probe: correlate kernel_signature across slow traces; check compile counts and fallback kernels.
H4: Batching or queueing change increased tail latency
  - Probe: histogram request_end_to_end.seconds by batch_size and serving.pool_queue depth; inspect queue drain events.
H5: Downstream postprocessing or safety filters changed output
  - Probe: toggle postprocess filter log-level or run raw decode-only path for test tenant (if safe).

Sample quick queries (Grafana/BigQuery/Datadog style pseudocode)
- Top-10 tenants by p99 token latency last 15m:
  SELECT tenant_id, quantile(0.99, token_latency) as p99 FROM token_latencies WHERE ts > now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY p99 DESC LIMIT 10
- KV heatmap: last access time per model_shard (windowed):
  SELECT model_shard, minute_bucket(last_access_ts, 1) as minute, count(*) FROM kv_access_logs WHERE ts > now() - interval '60 minutes' GROUP BY model_shard, minute ORDER BY model_shard, minute
- Sample traces matching slow decode path:
  FROM traces WHERE service = 'serving.exec' AND span_duration > 1.5s AND tags['model_id'] = 'open-llm-7b' SELECT trace_id, spans ORDER BY span_duration DESC LIMIT 50

Dashboard snippets: what to show in a compact incident slate
- Header: incident id, reported by, short symptom, model_id, timeframe, operator owner
- Row 1: Latency quantiles timeline (p50/p90/p99) + traffic rate
- Row 2: Error counts by type + variant split bar chart
- Row 3: KV warmth sparkline and eviction spikes (same time window)
- Row 4: Trace waterfall mini-gallery (3 failing vs 3 baseline) with annotated key spans
- Row 5: Inline sample outputs and quick notes (copyable)

Operator quick recipes (copyable steps):
- If p99 token latency > baseline by >30%: collect 10 sample trace IDs, run slice by kernel_signature and GPU type.
- If kv_cache_hitrate drops >50% for a tenant: run a warm-probe job that issues 100 golden prompts and confirm warming.
- If request_errors spike and type=model_oom: capture GPU_free_memory at span start for 20 failed traces and escalate to infra with 'oom-bulk' tag.

Data-retention & evidence packaging guidance:
- Keep full traces for incident window + 2 hours (hot) and export raw spans to evidence bundle (S3) for long-term forensic (7–30 days depending on severity).
- Attach the following to ticket: 10 trace IDs (failing), 3 baseline trace IDs, kv_access_snippet.csv (last-touch list), dashboard permalink, sampled outputs.txt, model rollout commit id.

Open questions / TODOs (workshop list):
- Define a compact "generation_quality" score schema owned by eval team (how to compare cross-model fairly).
- Lightweight trace exporter that redacts PII automatically for quick evidence sharing.
- A dashboard template that operators can instantiate from incident UI with prefilled widgets above.

Appendix A — Minimal ticket template (copy/paste):
- short_summary:
- first_reported_by:
- symptom_description (include exact prompt or sample corpus):
- model_id / model_variant / rollout_tag / commit_sha:
- timeframe_start / timeframe_end:
- 10 failing_trace_ids (comma separated):
- kv_cache_snapshot_location (S3):
- quick_notes_and_hypotheses:

Appendix B — Example span property table (for engineers):
- span.name: serving.exec
- attr.model_id: open-llm-7b
- attr.kernel_signature: conv-opt-v3
- attr.kv_cache_hit: false
- attr.decode_time_ms: 1245
- attr.gpu_free_mb: 1200

Notes to self (operator shorthand):
- Keep the ad-hoc dashboard narrow. Too many panels -> noise. Start with latency, kv warmth, variant split, trace gallery, outputs.
- Always capture raw outputs (not just scores) — human review is quickest initial signal.
- If sampling budget is tight, prefer trace capture for slow tails and kv-access logs for heatmap reconstruction.

End of playbook.
